name: email-san-no-at-invalid
description: permittedSubtrees rfc822Name is 'example.com' (host-form constraint). The leaf's rfc822Name SAN is 'not-an-email.example' — a value with no '@' character at all. RFC 5321 mandates that a mailbox contain exactly one '@' separating the local-part from the domain. A SAN that's not a valid mailbox cannot be matched by the constraint and the leaf must be rejected, either at parse time (UNSUPPORTED_NAME_SYNTAX) or at constraint time (no plausible parse satisfies the host-form constraint).
notes: Companion to email-multiple-at-raw-san-invalid (which tests multi-'@' SANs). Constructed via unknown_extensions raw DER because cryptography's RFC822Name API rejects values lacking an '@'.

Probes whether a validator that does host-suffix matching on the constraint side handles the 'no at' SAN safely. A lax parser might treat the whole value as the host portion and accept; a strict parser rejects it as malformed.
